events.title: Government attorney moves to dismiss asylum cases in San Antonio court; judge grants one dismissal without stated reason
events.summary: At San Antonio immigration court, a government attorney moved to dismiss the cases of two single adults—a man and a woman—both seeking asylum or other relief. The judge granted the man's case dismissal even before the government attorney provided a reason. The judge then informed the man, using a Turkish interpreter, that he would likely be placed in expedited removal despite having entered the US more than two years earlier—beyond the legal threshold for expedited removal. The woman, who had been in the country for nearly four years and was applying for a visa for victims of serious crimes, was not represented by counsel. The judge threatened to order her repatriation but the government attorney "saved" her by requesting dismissal instead. Both individuals were apprehended by ICE agents immediately after leaving the courtroom.
events.why_relevant: A judge dismissing a case without stated reason, threatening repatriation of an unrepresented migrant, and coordinating with government attorneys to dismiss cases immediately before ICE apprehension demonstrates the collapse of judicial independence and the subordination of courts to executive enforcement priorities.
events.basis: The judge granted the man's case even before the government attorney had given a reason why" and "the judge was upset with her for not also filing an asylum application, and he threatened to order her repatriated

events.title: Chicago immigration court attendance plummets as ICE arrests deter migrants from appearing
events.summary: ICE plainclothes officers have been documented attending immigration court in Chicago with target lists, apprehending court attendees regardless of whether their cases are dismissed. Detainees are transported to detention facilities in Missouri, Florida, and Texas—often far from family and support networks. The lag in ICE's online detainee locator has caused some detainees to effectively disappear from public tracking. As word of these arrests has spread through immigrant communities, court attendance has dropped dramatically, creating a secondary enforcement effect: migrants now avoid court appearances entirely, risking automatic deportation orders for no-shows.
events.why_relevant: The use of courthouse arrests as a deterrent has created a chilling effect that prevents migrants from exercising their legal right to appear in court, effectively denying them access to judicial process and due process protections while simultaneously creating conditions for automatic deportation orders based on non-appearance.
events.basis: Spiro of the NIJC, meanwhile, works in Chicago and said she and fellow advocates have documented Ice officers in plainclothes coming to immigration court there with a list of whom they're targeting – and court attendees are apprehended whether or not their case is dismissed

events.title: Iowa completes noncitizen voter verification after court ruling
events.summary: Following a court ruling that allowed the investigation to proceed, Iowa conducted a comprehensive review of more than 2,000 voters initially flagged for potential ineligibility based on outdated DMV records. events.title: Trump proclaimed 50% tariff on copper semi-finished and derivative products, effective August 1, 2025, citing national security under Section 232.
events.summary: President Trump issued Proclamation 10962 imposing a 50 percent tariff on semi-finished copper products and intensive copper derivative products, effective August 1, 2025. The proclamation invokes Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, based on a Commerce Department report finding that copper imports threaten U.S. national security. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for including additional copper derivatives within 90 days and to monitor domestic copper markets for potential future action on refined copper tariffs (15 percent starting 2027, 30 percent starting 2028). Domestic sales requirements for copper input materials and high-quality copper scrap are to be implemented under the Defense Production Act.

events.title: Trump suspends duty-free de minimis treatment globally, imposing tariffs on all low-value imports
events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14324 on July 30, 2025, suspending the duty-free de minimis exemption for all shipments regardless of value or country of origin, effective August 29, 2025. The order invokes national emergencies declared under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) related to drug trafficking from Canada, Mexico, and China, and trade deficits. All articles previously exempt from duties under 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) will now be subject to applicable duties, taxes, and fees. The Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to implement the order through regulatory changes and notices in the Federal Register.

events.title: EPA approves Wyoming regional haze State Implementation Plan revision for Jim Bridger power plant units
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency approved Wyoming's December 2022 State Implementation Plan revision addressing regional haze visibility protection at Jim Bridger Units 1 and 2. The approval replaces previous nitrogen oxide emission limits (0.07 lb/MMBtu) with new limits (0.12 lb/MMBtu) and associated heat input caps, finding them sufficient for reasonable progress during the first implementation period. The rule also approves monthly and annual NOx and SO2 emission limits for all four Jim Bridger units and becomes effective September 8, 2025.
events.why_relevant: This final rule modifies federal air-quality standards for a major power plant, affecting visibility protection in national parks and wilderness areas under the Clean Air Act's regional haze program.
events.basis: The EPA is approving a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision submitted by the State of Wyoming on December 30, 2022, and supplemented on August 31, 2023, and November 16, 2023, addressing regional haze for Jim Bridger Units 1 and 2.
